subfiles.about: Memorandum from Assistant Secretary Hilldring to Secretary Marshall summarizing interdepartmental disagreements over the territorial disposition of the Ryukyu Islands and requesting authorization to negotiate with the War and Navy Departments.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring asks Marshall to approve State's position that the Ryukyus return to Japan demilitarized, against the military's wish for a strategic trusteeship. Marshall approves informal talks but doubts the military case can be ignored.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum from General Hilldring to the Secretary on United States Position Reference Ryukyu Islands

subfiles.about: Attachment detailing the political, legal, and diplomatic arguments formulated in SWNCC 59/1 supporting Japan's retention of the Ryukyu Islands.
subfiles.summary: Tab A gives State's arguments for Japan keeping the Ryukyus: historic ties since 1879, U.S. principles, Soviet suspicion and the cost of governing 840,000 people.
subfiles.title: Political Arguments for Retention of the Ryukyu Islands by Japan (Tab A)
